question: In which of the following years was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in **1878** by Lord Lytton, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The Act was aimed at curbing the freedom of the Indian-language press and was considered a repressive measure.
 
• It empowered the government to confiscate the printing presses, paper, and other materials of the native press if it published anything that was deemed seditious.
 
• The Act was specifically targeted at the Indian press and excluded the English-language publications.
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was repealed in **1882** by Lord Ripon, who succeeded Lord Lytton as Viceroy of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the Act:**

 
 
• The growing influence of the Indian press during the 1870s led the British government to introduce the Vernacular Press Act to control anti-British sentiments.
 
• Indian newspapers had started to criticize British policies, which alarmed the colonial administration.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Journalism:**
 
 
• The Act imposed severe restrictions on the Indian press, leading to widespread protests and resentment among Indian journalists and nationalists.
 
• It marked a significant moment in the history of the Indian freedom struggle, emphasizing the need for freedom of expression.
 
 
 
• **Repeal of the Act:**
 
 
• Lord Ripon, known for his liberal policies, repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882, restoring press freedom to some extent.
 
• This repeal was welcomed by Indian leaders and helped to reduce some of the tensions between the British government and the Indian populace.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Vernacular Press Act is often cited as an example of colonial repression, and its history is studied in the context of the freedom of the press in India.
 
• It remains a significant event that highlighted the power of the press and its role in shaping public opinion.
